Commercial coffee roasting involves controlled pyrolysis of green coffee beans through a temperature profile with three (3) distinct phases: (1) drying (ambient to approx. 150C, duration 4-8 min, moisture reduction from 10-12% to below 5%), (2) Maillard reaction and caramelization (150-200C, sugar browning and amino acid reactions producing flavor precursors), and (3) first crack and development (200-230C, exothermic reaction accompanied by audible cracking as internal steam pressure exceeds cell wall strength). Roast degree is quantified using colorimetry (Agtron scale, 0-100, where lower values indicate darker roasts) or by weight loss percentage (typically 12-20% depending on roast level). Specialty coffee (as defined by SCA, Specialty Coffee Association) scores 80+ on a 100-point cupping scale. Extraction during brewing targets 18-22% of soluble solids (measured by TDS, total dissolved solids, using a refractometer). Water temperature should be maintained at 92-96C with a brew ratio of approximately 1:15 to 1:18 (coffee to water, by mass).
